messages:
ravi: Hey folks, first day! I accepted the org invite but private repos show a 403 and a banner saying SSO + 2FA required. I actually set up 2FA with a hardware key (YubiKey) yesterday and can login fine, but `git clone` is blocked. I also tried a PAT from my work account and it failed. Any ideas?

it-bot: Org policy: SAML SSO (Okta) + 2FA required. Personal or pre-SSO PATs may be blocked; you need to authorize org SSO for the account and use work credentials. https://github.com/orgs/redwood-inference/sso :robot_face: 

maria: welcome @ravi! quick checks: is the GH account email the primary (not an alias)? GH often ignores plus-address aliases for org provisioning. Check https://github.com/settings/emails to confirm the exact primary verified email.

ravi: i used ravi+eng@redwood.com when creating the account (that's forwarded to ravi@redwood.com). GH shows both addresses but the primary is ravi@redwood.com. Could that mismatch matter?

infra: yes — if the org invite went to ravi+eng@redwood.com but your primary GH email is ravi@redwood.com the SSO link might attach to the alias and cause a mismatch. Two options: 1) make the invited address the primary/verified on GH, or 2) have an admin re-send invite to the primary. I'll check which email the invite used.

ravi: i also clicked the SSO authorize banner while signed in. `gh auth status` output:
```
github.com: Logged in to github.com as ravi@redwood (Session active)
  Git operations for github.com: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-templates (permission: none)
```

devrel: that permission: none line suggests SSO didn't attach properly to the account used for git ops. If you can, set the invited email as primary temporarily, re-authorize SSO, then switch primary back. Or infra can re-provision on their side.

infra: i looked up the invite and it was sent to ravi+eng@redwood.com. I just re-sent the invite to ravi@redwood.com and forced a membership sync for your account. Try signing out/in and re-click the authorize button on the org page.

ravi: signed out, signed back in, clicked authorize. Still getting `Permission denied (publickey)` when trying `git clone` with SSH. But `ssh -T git@github.com` says `Hi ravi! You've successfully authenticated` so the key is OK.

ops-bot: Note: organization blocks tokens that were created before SSO enforcement. If you used a PAT, revoke and re-create it after authorizing SSO, or better use `gh auth login` / SSH keys.

maria: also check if VS Code / CI stored an old token somewhere. Run `gh auth status --show-token` to see which token is active for CLI, and `grep -R \"github.com\" ~/.config 2>/dev/null` to find cached tokens.

ravi: `gh auth status --show-token` shows a token but CLI still reports permission none for the repo. I revoked the old PAT from settings, re-ran `gh auth login` and re-added my SSH key with `gh ssh-key add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub --title \"work laptop\"`.

infra: i forced another sync and explicitly added your GH username to the `onboarding` and `infra-templates` teams. Wait ~30s and try clone again.

ravi: clone now works! `git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/infra-templates.git` succeeded. Thanks all. Two notes: (1) hardware 2FA is fine, but PATs must be recreated after SSO authorize, (2) invited-to-email alias vs primary email can cause confusion.

devrel: awesome — we'll add a short blurb to the onboarding doc: "If your account uses an email alias, ensure the invited address is primary/verified or ask infra to re-send invite; recreate PATs after authorizing SSO; prefer SSH or `gh auth login`." :memo: 

ravi: saved that and left a comment in the onboarding doc. Appreciate the quick help! :tada:
